The Empire State Building went up in about 410 days. At its peak, 4½ floors a week. Here's how, in 40 seconds. ⏱️

A hotel torn down. A 55-foot hole. 57,000 tons of steel. A limestone and aluminium skin.

And the twist: the spire on top was built as a docking mast for airships. It was far too windy, and it was never used. 🎈

Next: the Colosseum. Follow so you don't miss it. 👇

yt_title: How the Empire State Building Was Built: 410 Days in 40 Seconds #shorts
yt_description:
Demolition of the old Waldorf–Astoria, a 55-ft foundation, 57,480 tons of steel rising up to 4.5 floors a week, an Indiana limestone and aluminium facade, and a mast designed for docking airships that winds made impossible to use.

The Empire State Building (1930–1931), the world's tallest building for 39 years, built in 40 seconds.

Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_State_Building
Figures are historical estimates. Animation is a stylised reconstruction.
